newsitem.title: USA: Airborne Express gives optimistic outlook.
newsitem.headline: Airborne Express gives optimistic outlook.

text.p: Airborne Express' operating results should remain strong as long as there are no negative changes in the economy or competitive environment for the rest of the year, said Airborne's chief financial officer Roy Liljebeck.
"Operating results in the first quarter were stronger than they have been for some time," he said after Monday's release of Airborne's first quarter results.
"The operating margin of 4.9 percent resulted from a number of positive factors, including steady growth in domestic shipments."

"The growth in domestic business continues to be strongest in higher-yielding overnight business...while the growth in international revenues is modest, the operating margins on international business continue at a much faster rate than revenue," Liljebeck added.
The cost of aviation fuel continued to exceed the price experienced in the first quarter of 1996 by 11.8 cents per gallon.
"Fortunately, the implementation of a two percent fuel surcharge on February 17, 1997, and the proceeds from fuel hedging in the quarter, offset the increased cost," he said.
A moratorium on aviation excise tax from January 1-March 6 resulted in a $4.3 million benefit in the first quarter.
